writing.title: Email: cambio de horario de tutoría
writing.prompt:
**Situación.** You have a tutorial with your academic advisor, Dr. Evans, on Thursday at 10:00, but you have just learned that you must take a required lab session at the same time.

**Write an email to Dr. Evans.** In your email, do the following:
- Explain why you cannot attend the tutorial.
- Suggest two alternative times.
- Ask what you should prepare in advance.
checklist: Saludo y propósito en la primera oración
Los tres puntos del enunciado cubiertos
Tono cortés (would, could, I would appreciate)
Releí para corregir concordancia y artículos
writing.model:
Dear Dr. Evans,

I am writing to ask whether we could reschedule our tutorial on Thursday at 10:00. I have just learned that a required lab session has been scheduled at the same time, and I am not able to miss it.

Would it be possible to meet on Wednesday afternoon after 2:00 or on Friday morning before 11:00? I am happy to adapt to whichever time suits you best.

In addition, could you tell me what I should prepare before we meet? If it would help, I can send you my draft outline in advance.

Thank you very much for your understanding.

Kind regards,
Maria Lopez

writing.title: Email: queja por un servicio de residencia
writing.prompt:
**Situación.** The heating in your university residence room has not worked for four days. You already told the front desk twice, but nothing has changed.

**Write an email to the housing office.** In your email:
- Describe the problem and what you already did.
- Explain how it is affecting you.
- Request a specific solution and a timeline.
writing.model:
Dear Housing Office,

I am writing about a problem in my room, number 214. The heating has not worked for four days. I reported it to the front desk on Monday and again on Wednesday, but nobody has come to repair it.

Because temperatures are very low at night, I have difficulty sleeping and studying in my room, and I am worried about getting ill before my exams.

Could you please arrange for a technician to visit within the next 24 hours? If the repair will take longer, I would appreciate a temporary heater in the meantime.

Thank you for your prompt attention.

Sincerely,
Carlos Ruiz

writing.title: Email: pedir una carta de recomendación
writing.prompt:
**Situación.** You are applying for a master's programme and need a recommendation letter from Professor Martin, who taught your thesis seminar last year.

**Write an email to Professor Martin.** In your email:
- Remind the professor who you are.
- Ask politely for the letter and give the deadline.
- Offer to send supporting materials.
checklist: La petición es cortés y concreta
writing.model:
Dear Professor Martin,

I hope you are well. I was a student in your thesis seminar last spring, where I presented a project on urban water systems.

I am applying to a master's programme in Water Engineering, and I was wondering whether you would be willing to write a letter of recommendation for me. The deadline is 20 December, and the letter would be submitted through an online form.

I would be glad to send you my CV, my statement of purpose and a short summary of my seminar project to make the process easier.

Thank you very much for considering my request.

Best regards,
Ana Torres

writing.title: Email: disculpa por faltar a un trabajo en grupo
writing.prompt:
**Situación.** You missed a group meeting yesterday because you were sick. Your teammate Priya is organizing the project.

**Write an email to Priya.** In your email:
- Apologize and briefly explain.
- Ask what you missed.
- Offer a way to make up your part of the work.
writing.model:
Hi Priya,

I am very sorry that I missed our meeting yesterday. I woke up with a high fever and could not leave my room.

Could you tell me what you decided and whether the task distribution changed? If there are notes, I would be grateful if you could share them.

To make up for it, I can write the first draft of the literature review by Friday evening and take on an extra section of the slides.

Thanks for understanding, and sorry again.

Best,
Diego

writing.title: Foro: ¿clases en línea o presenciales?
writing.prompt:
**Professor Hall:** This week we are discussing the future of university education. Some argue that most lectures should be moved online, while others think in-person classes are essential. What is your view, and why?

**Sam:** Online lectures let students learn at their own pace and rewatch difficult parts. I think universities should record everything.

**Lena:** I disagree. Being in the room helps me ask questions and meet other students. Online-only learning feels isolating.

**Write a response** that contributes your own opinion to the discussion (at least 100 words). Include a reason and an example, and refer to what Sam or Lena said.
checklist: Opinión clara en la primera o segunda oración
writing.model:
I agree with Sam that recorded lectures are extremely useful, but I do not think they should replace in-person classes entirely. A mixed approach seems best.

First, recordings give students control. For example, when I studied thermodynamics, I rewatched the same explanation three times until I understood it, something impossible in a live class. However, as Lena points out, a classroom offers spontaneous questions and discussion, and these are often where deep understanding develops.

Furthermore, group projects are easier when students know each other in person. Therefore, universities could record lectures but keep seminars and labs on campus. In this way, students would benefit from flexibility without losing human contact.

writing.title: Foro: ¿exámenes o proyectos?
writing.prompt:
**Professor Ortiz:** Many courses assess students with a final exam, while others use projects. Which method better shows what a student has learned? Explain your opinion.

**Kai:** Projects are better because they let us apply knowledge to real problems.

**Dina:** Exams are fairer because everyone has the same conditions and nobody can get too much help.

**Write a response** with your opinion, one reason and one example (at least 100 words). Mention Kai or Dina.
writing.model:
In my view, projects show learning more accurately, although exams still have a role. Kai is right that projects require students to apply ideas, not just remember them.

For instance, in my programming course we had to build a small application for a local library. Solving real problems forced us to plan, test and explain our decisions, which is exactly what employers expect. In contrast, my memory of the exam content faded within weeks.

However, Dina makes a fair point about equal conditions. To address this, instructors could combine both methods: a short exam for the basics and a project for deeper skills. This balance would be fair and meaningful.

writing.title: Foro: ¿cuánto deben trabajar los estudiantes?
writing.prompt:
**Professor Nguyen:** Some students work part-time while studying. Is this a good idea, or should students focus only on their studies?

**Omar:** Working teaches responsibility and helps with money problems.

**Julia:** A job takes time away from studying and can hurt grades.

**Write a response** (at least 100 words) with your opinion, a reason and an example.
writing.model:
I believe a limited part-time job can be beneficial, as long as it does not exceed about ten hours a week. Omar is correct that work teaches responsibility; for example, my cousin learned to manage her time much better after she started tutoring.

On the other hand, Julia's concern is also valid. A job with long hours leaves little energy for reading and assignments. Consequently, grades may suffer, which defeats the purpose of studying.

Therefore, students should choose flexible, short jobs, preferably related to their field, such as a research assistant position. In this way, they gain experience and income without sacrificing their studies.

writing.title: Foro: ¿la tecnología distrae en clase?
writing.prompt:
**Professor Adams:** Should laptops and phones be allowed during lectures?

**Elena:** Laptops help me take faster, organized notes, so they should be allowed.

**Tom:** Screens distract everyone nearby. I think devices should be banned.

**Write a response** (at least 100 words) with your opinion, a reason and an example.
writing.model:
I think laptops should be allowed, but phones should not. Elena is right that typing makes notes faster; for example, in my statistics class, I could copy formulas accurately instead of missing them.

However, Tom's concern about distraction is serious, because a nearby screen showing videos attracts attention. A reasonable rule would be to allow laptops only in the first rows and to forbid phones. Moreover, instructors could ask students to close the lid during discussions.

In short, a clear policy that protects both note-taking and concentration is better than a complete ban.

questions.q: Why did you choose the field you want to study?
questions.model: I chose engineering because I enjoy solving practical problems. For example, last year I built a small irrigation system for my family's garden, and I loved seeing it work.

questions.q: How do you usually prepare for an important exam?
questions.model: I start two weeks early and make a schedule. For example, I review one chapter a day and then test myself with practice questions, which shows me my weak points.

questions.q: What do you do to relax after a stressful week?
questions.model: I usually go for a long walk or play football with friends. It clears my mind, and afterwards I can focus much better on my work.

questions.q: Do you prefer studying alone or with other students? Why?
questions.model: I prefer a mix. Alone, I concentrate better on reading, but with others I can check my understanding. For example, explaining a concept to a classmate shows me what I still do not know.

questions.q: How has technology changed the way people study?
questions.model: It has made information available instantly. For example, I can watch a lecture from another university at midnight, which was impossible for my parents.

questions.q: Do you think people spend too much time on their phones? Explain.
questions.model: Yes, in many cases. I notice friends checking messages during meals, and it reduces real conversation. Setting limits can help.

questions.q: What is one invention you could not live without?
questions.model: The bicycle, because it is cheap, fast in the city and good for health. I use it every day to reach campus.

questions.q: Would you like to work with robots or artificial intelligence in the future? Why?
questions.model: Yes, because they can do repetitive tasks and let people focus on creative work. For instance, an assistant that sorts data would save me hours.

questions.q: How do you usually get to your university or workplace?
questions.model: I take the bus because it is reliable and cheap. It takes about thirty minutes, and I use the time to read.

questions.q: What would make your city a better place to live?
questions.model: More green spaces and safer bike lanes. For example, a bike lane on my street would let many more people avoid traffic.

questions.q: Do you think public transportation should be free? Why or why not?
questions.model: I think it should be cheap rather than completely free. Free service can reduce pollution, but it needs funding to stay reliable.

questions.q: Would you rather live in a big city or a small town?
questions.model: A mid-sized city, because it offers opportunities without being overwhelming. I like having a library and cafés nearby but also quiet parks.

questions.q: Why is learning English important for your future plans?
questions.model: English is the language of science and many master's programmes. For me, it is the key to studying abroad and reading research papers.

questions.q: What is the most difficult part of learning a new language?
questions.model: For me, listening to fast speech. People link words together, so I practice with podcasts and repeat sentences aloud.

questions.q: Do you think it is better to study grammar or to practice speaking first?
questions.model: Both are needed, but I would start speaking early. Mistakes are useful feedback, and grammar becomes clearer after you try to use it.

questions.q: What advice would you give to someone starting English today?
questions.model: Study a little every day and use English for something you enjoy, such as videos or games. Consistency matters more than long sessions.

questions.q: Describe a time when you worked well in a team.
questions.model: In a design project last year, we divided tasks by strengths and met twice a week. We finished early because everyone communicated clearly.

questions.q: What qualities make a good team leader?
questions.model: Good leaders listen first and make clear decisions. For example, my best supervisor asked for ideas and then explained why we chose one.

questions.q: How do you handle disagreements with classmates?
questions.model: I stay calm and ask for the reasons behind their view. Usually we find a compromise by testing both ideas.

questions.q: Is it better to have a fixed leader or to share leadership?
questions.model: Shared leadership works in small, experienced groups, but a fixed leader helps when deadlines are tight, because decisions are faster.

questions.q: What do you do to stay healthy while studying?
questions.model: I sleep at least seven hours and exercise three times a week. Both help my memory and concentration.

questions.q: Do you think students should have more time for sports at university?
questions.model: Yes, because exercise reduces stress. A short daily break for sport could improve results too.

questions.q: How important is sleep for academic success?
questions.model: Very important. When I stay up late, I forget what I learned, so I now study earlier and sleep well.

questions.q: What is your opinion about energy drinks and coffee for studying?
questions.model: A little coffee helps, but too much causes anxiety. I prefer water and short breaks.

questions.q: What can individuals do to protect the environment?
questions.model: They can reduce waste, use public transport and save energy. Small habits, multiplied by millions, make a real difference.

questions.q: Do you think universities should teach sustainability to all students?
questions.model: Yes, because every profession affects resources. A short common course would give everyone the basics.

questions.q: What environmental problem worries you most in your country?
questions.model: Water scarcity worries me because it affects farming and cities. Better infrastructure and awareness are needed.

questions.q: Would you pay more for products that are better for the environment?
questions.model: Yes, within reason. If the label is trustworthy, I would pay a little more because it benefits everyone in the long run.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself five years from now?
questions.model: I hope to be working as an engineer on sustainable energy projects, maybe in Europe, after finishing my master's.

questions.q: What is the biggest challenge of studying in another country?
questions.model: Probably adapting to a new language and culture. I plan to join student groups to make friends quickly.

questions.q: What skill would you like to improve this year? Why?
questions.model: Speaking confidently in English, because presentations and group work depend on it. I practice a few minutes every day.

questions.q: How do you stay motivated when a goal takes a long time?
questions.model: I break the goal into small steps and track progress. Seeing my streak grow keeps me going.
